title: The Bloch sphere as a map of pure states
objectives: Translate pure-state amplitudes to a Bloch point up to global phase.
Interpret poles, relative phase and measurement probabilities.
prerequisites: Chapter 3’s complex amplitudes, normalization, inner products and projectors; Chapter 2’s probability and count distinction.

quizzes.question: If the Bloch z-coordinate is −1/2, what is PZ(1)?
feedback: A coordinate can be negative; a probability cannot.

quizzes.question: At the south pole, do different phi values specify different pure-qubit states?
options: Yes, all angles are physically different.
No; the remaining component changes only by a global phase.
feedback: The 0 component vanishes, so this azimuth is not a distinct physical direction.
Correct. Relative phase between two nonzero components is unavailable here.
The sign convention for angles does not change the pole.
